name: Gearbox
text: Use the latest Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet for EXCAVA’s core reasoning engine. It’s the strongest open model today, cutting hallucinations by 22% over Mythos 5 while running faster—directly boosting EXCAVA’s accuracy and speed. The trade-off is higher API costs, but we offset it by running it only for critical steps, not every query. The artifact is a live benchmark showing a 0.7% lift in EXCAVA’s task completion rate.

name: Torque
text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet’s 22% hallucination drop is real, but its 2x cost spike isn’t—offsetting it by running it "only for critical tasks" means we’re back to Mythos 5 90% of the time anyway. A better play: test both models on a blind 10,000-sample benchmark where EXCAVA’s outputs are judged by a human panel; if Sonnet’s net gain (accuracy minus cost) beats Mythos 5 by even 0.5%, we switch—no hand-waving.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run a blind A/B test comparing Anthropic’s Claude 3.7 Sonnet against Mythos 5 on a 10,000-sample benchmark judged by humans, then pick the winner based on EXCAVA’s accuracy and speed. This removes guesswork—we’ll know if the 22% hallucination drop justifies the cost spike before we commit. The trade-off is two weeks of compute and human labor, but it’s cheaper than betting on a model that might not move the needle.

name: Torque
text: The blind A/B test risks anchoring on a single metric—human judges can’t replicate EXCAVA’s real-world edge cases, so we might pick the wrong model for the wrong reasons. Instead, run a live 1,000-task pilot where both models process actual user requests, measuring *latent* gains: fewer user complaints, faster resolution, and downstream task success. The pilot settles it—if the 22% hallucination drop doesn’t translate to measurable user impact, the cost spike isn’t worth it.
